sections.h2: How many days of notice does a Nebraska landlord have to give?
sections.html:
The number of days depends on the reason: 7 days for unpaid rent, 14 or 30 days for a lease violation, 5 days for serious safety problems, and 30 days to end a month-to-month tenancy. Each notice must be in writing.

ReasonWritten noticeCan the tenant fix it?Statute
Rent not paid7 calendar daysYes, by paying within the 7 days76-1431(2)
Material lease breachEnds not less than 30 days after receipt if not remedied in 14 daysYes, within 14 days76-1431(1)
Same breach again within 6 monthsAt least 14 daysNo cure period76-1431(1)
Violent crime, illegal drug sales, threats to safety5 daysNo right to cure76-1431(4)
Month-to-month, no cause30 days before the rental dateNot applicable76-1437(2)
Week-to-week, no cause7 days before the end dateNot applicable76-1437(1)

The notice only starts the process. A landlord who wants the tenant out still has to go to court.

sections.h2: What must a nonpayment notice say?
sections.html:
It must tell the tenant that rent is unpaid and that the landlord intends to end the rental agreement if the rent is not paid within seven calendar days. Both statements matter, because the statute ties the right to terminate to written notice of nonpayment and of that intention.

If the tenant pays in full inside the seven days, the landlord has no basis to terminate on that notice. Rent unpaid after the period lets the landlord end the agreement and move to the court step described below.

Nebraska's wording is a seven-day calendar count and not a business-day count, so weekends and holidays are included. Keep proof of how and when the notice was delivered, since the complaint later has to show compliance with the notice rules.

sections.h2: What is the difference between the 14-day and 30-day lease violation notice?
sections.html:
They are two parts of one notice. The landlord must give a written notice describing the acts or omissions that make up the breach, and the agreement ends on a date at least 30 days after the tenant receives it unless the tenant fixes the problem within 14 days.

The statute covers a noncompliance with the tenant's duties that materially affects health and safety, or a material breach of the rental agreement. If the breach can be remedied by repairs, paying damages or otherwise, and the tenant does so before the date in the notice, the agreement does not terminate.

  • A repeat of substantially the same problem within six months allows termination on at least 14 days' written notice, with no new chance to cure.
  • The landlord may also recover damages and seek an injunction for noncompliance.
  • If the tenant's noncompliance is willful, reasonable attorney's fees can be recovered.

sections.h2: When can a Nebraska landlord use the five-day notice?
sections.html:
The five-day notice applies when the tenant, a household member, a guest or anyone under the tenant's control engages in violent criminal activity, the illegal sale of a controlled substance, or other activity that threatens the health or safety of other tenants, the landlord or the landlord's employees. The tenant has no right to cure.

The statute lists examples that include physical assault or the threat of it, illegal use of a firearm or other weapon, possession of a controlled substance the tenant knew or should have known about, and conduct that threatens or causes property damage. The complaint must describe the incidents behind the suit.

There is a protection for tenants who are not the source of the problem. A landlord may not use this notice when the activity is by someone other than the tenant or a household member and the tenant takes steps such as seeking a protective order or reporting it to law enforcement. A perpetrator of domestic violence is not covered by that protection.

sections.h2: How does a month-to-month tenancy end without a reason?
sections.html:
Either side can end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice given at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice. A week-to-week tenancy needs at least seven days' written notice before the termination date.

If a lease has no fixed term, Nebraska treats the tenancy as month to month, or week to week for a roomer who pays weekly. That default can matter for a seller who inherited a house with someone living in it and no written lease.

A tenant who stays after the term or after termination without the landlord's consent can be sued for possession. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, the landlord may also recover up to three months' periodic rent or threefold actual damages, whichever is greater, plus reasonable attorney's fees.

sections.h2: What happens in court after the notice period ends?
sections.html:
The landlord files a complaint for restitution with the clerk of the district or county court. The complaint must state the statutory authority for possession, the specific facts, a reasonably accurate description of the premises and the compliance with the notice rules.

  1. The court issues a summons with a copy of the complaint. It must be served within three days, not counting nonjudicial days, and is returnable within five days, not counting nonjudicial days.
  2. The case is tried by the judge without a jury.
  3. If judgment goes against the tenant, the court declares the rental agreement forfeited.
  4. At the landlord's request, the court issues a writ of restitution directing the constable or sheriff to restore possession on a date no more than ten days after the writ issues.

Only an officer under a writ returns possession. A notice alone does not change who has the right to be in the house.

sections.h2: What limits does Nebraska put on retaliation?
sections.html:
A landlord may not raise rent, cut services or bring or threaten an action for possession in response to a tenant complaining to a housing or building code agency about a violation that materially affects health and safety, or joining a tenants' union. A tenant who proves this has a defense to the possession case.

The same statute lists situations where the landlord can still sue. Those are when the code violation was caused mainly by the tenant's lack of reasonable care, when the tenant is behind on rent, or when compliance would need work that deprives the tenant of the unit. Reasonable rent increases remain allowed.

If a tenant dies, the landlord must make a reasonable attempt within ten days to reach the person the tenant named to retrieve belongings. That person then has 20 days after contact to say they will claim the property and 20 more days to remove it.

sections.h2: What does an eviction mean if you also want to sell the house?
sections.html:
An owner with a tenant has three paths: finish the notice and court process before listing, sell with the tenant in place, or sell to a buyer who takes the house as it stands. Which one fits depends on the lease, the stage of the case and how soon you need to close.

  • Keep copies of the lease, rent ledger, every notice and the proof of delivery.
  • Check whether the complaint, judgment or writ is still open, because those papers affect what a buyer is willing to take on.
  • For a deed recorded on or after July 18, 2026, plan for the $3.32 per $1,000 documentary stamp tax and a Form 521 filing.

This page summarizes Nebraska's Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act notice rules and is not legal advice. Check the current statutes or speak with a Nebraska attorney before serving a notice.

faqs.q: How long is a Nebraska eviction notice for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven calendar days. The landlord must give written notice of nonpayment and the intent to terminate, and the tenant can stop the termination by paying within that time.

faqs.q: Can a Nebraska landlord evict without going to court?
faqs.a: No. After the notice period the landlord must file a complaint for restitution, and only a constable or sheriff acting on a writ of restitution restores possession.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to leave after a judgment?
faqs.a: The writ of restitution must set a possession date no more than ten days after the writ is issued. The court issues it at the landlord's request after judgment.

faqs.q: What notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Nebraska?
faqs.a: Written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice. Either the landlord or the tenant can give it, with no reason required.

faqs.q: Does the tenant get a chance to fix a lease violation?
faqs.a: Yes, for most violations. The tenant has 14 days to remedy, and the agreement ends at least 30 days after receipt if the breach is not fixed. A repeat of the same breach within six months allows 14 days' notice without a cure period.

faqs.q: Is there a shorter notice for dangerous behavior?
faqs.a: Yes. Violent criminal activity, illegal sale of controlled substances or activity that threatens safety allows suit for possession after five days' written notice, with no right to cure.

faqs.q: Can a landlord retaliate if a tenant reports code violations?
faqs.a: Not by raising rent, reducing services or threatening a possession action over a health and safety code complaint, though the landlord can still sue for unpaid rent or other listed exceptions.
